::error file=src/api/cart.ts,line=4,col=1,title=4layers/layer-dependency::infrastructure may not import application ("@/stores/cart" resolves to src/stores/cart.ts). infrastructure may import: domain. Infrastructure should expose data and let application call it, not the other way round.
::error file=src/components/CartView.vue,line=13,col=1,title=4layers/layer-dependency::presentation may not import infrastructure ("@/api/cart" resolves to src/api/cart.ts). presentation may import: application, domain. Put the call in an application-layer store or composable and let the component consume that.
::error file=src/components/CartView.vue,line=15,col=1,title=4layers/package-boundary::The presentation layer may not import "axios". Move "axios" behind the application layer so the component only talks to state and use cases.
::error file=src/domain/order.ts,line=2,col=1,title=4layers/package-boundary::The domain layer may not import "vue". Keep the domain framework-agnostic: wrap "vue" in an infrastructure adapter and depend on a domain port instead.
::error file=src/domain/order.ts,line=3,col=1,title=4layers/layer-dependency::domain may not import infrastructure ("@/api/cart" resolves to src/api/cart.ts). domain may not import any other layer. Invert the dependency: declare a port (interface) in the domain and implement it in infrastructure.
